findings.situation: A filer whose item belongs on another line, such as staking income (line 8v), scholarship not on a W-2 (line 8r), or a taxable 1099-G amount already entered elsewhere, truthfully gives its full amount here, so it is counted on line 8z as well as on its own line.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8z: "Use line 8z to report any taxable income not reported elsewhere on your return or other schedules."
findings.why: The question asks for 'The amount of this item to include in income for 2025' and never says to leave out income reported on another line or schedule. Taxable income reported elsewhere gets counted twice.

findings.situation: A filer with a loss on a corrective distribution of excess deferrals must report a negative amount on line 8z, but the accepted answer only allows zero or more.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8z: "Examples of income to report on line 8z include the following. ... Loss on certain corrective distributions of excess deferrals."
findings.why: Line 8z takes this loss as a negative figure. NonNegDollars cannot hold it, and no listed refusal covers the case.
findings.bound: any dollar amount, negative allowed for losses such as on corrective distributions of excess deferrals

findings.situation: A filer whose charity sold donated property within 3 years truthfully picks charitable_recapture, so oi8z.additional_tax turns on even though the text applies interest and the additional 10% tax only to the fractional-interest recapture.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8z: "Recapture of a charitable contribution deduction relating to the contribution of a fractional interest in tangible personal property... Interest and an additional 10% tax apply to the amount of the recapture." vs. "Recapture of a charitable contribution deduction if the charitable organization disposes of the donated property within 3 years of the contribution. See Recapture if no exempt use in Pub. 526." Question option: "charitable_recapture (recapture of a charitable contribution deduction, for a fractional interest in tangible personal property or property the charity disposed of within 3 years)"
findings.why: The single choice merges two recapture types, but only the fractional-interest bullet carries the interest and additional 10% tax. The gate therefore flags an additional tax for the 3-year disposition recapture, which the text does not impose.
